claim.pdf_says: ACCESS MODE IS { SEQUENTIAL [RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1] / { RANDOM / [DYNAMIC] } RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1 } -- the level-2 box encloses only the keyword DYNAMIC; the closing brace of the inner RANDOM/DYNAMIC brace is printed outside the box
claim.why_it_matters: The level-2 box marker closes after the inner brace's closing glyph, so the markdown puts the inner brace close inside the level-2 box. The same format on page 438 renders it correctly as `║ <u>DYNAMIC</u> ║ ╯`. Syntax meaning (RANDOM or DYNAMIC, with DYNAMIC level 2) is unchanged; this is a figure-glyph placement defect only.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 440 (VIII-10, 2.4.2) shows the level-2 box drawn tightly around the underlined word DYNAMIC, with the inner brace's closing glyph outside the box. Markdown line 18 reads `║ <u>DYNAMIC</u> ╯ ║`, so the glyph order differs as claimed and both sources are quoted accurately. The difference does not change meaning. Both renderings carry the same syntax: ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL [RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1], or RANDOM/DYNAMIC (choose exactly one per §1985:IV.2.1.4 braces) followed by RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1, with only DYNAMIC marked as level 2. A brace-closing glyph has no level of its own, so where the box marker sits relative to it is pure figure-drawing placement. The claim itself admits that the meaning is unchanged, and the verification rules reject differences that do not change meaning.
